meta.title: HandyPlan · Stop losing jobs to missed calls
meta.description: When you're on a job and can't pick up, HandyPlan texts the caller back right away, asks what they need, and sends it to your phone as a job card. You pick a time and the job is booked. Free to use.
meta.ogDescription: Missed calls turned into booked jobs. Free for trade businesses.

problem.title: When you're working, nobody's in the office.
problem.subtitle: This is how most jobs get lost, and you never even hear about them.
steps: Someone's boiler breaks. They google a tradesperson and call the first name they find.
You're in a basement with your hands full. The phone rings out.
They don't leave a voicemail. They just call the next business on the list.
That job is gone, and you never knew it was there.
problem.claimTitle: A missed call is a lost job.
problem.claimBody: Most software promises to save you admin time. But you don't count your hours. You do notice when work goes to someone else.
problem.whyNow: 62% of trade businesses already call digitalisation one of their five biggest challenges (Bitkom Research, 2026). Being reachable is usually where it starts.
problem.fit: HandyPlan is for everyday calls, like a quote request or a routine repair. Real emergencies need a person on the phone, so those should always go to your emergency number.

why.title: Made for businesses that don't want another big software package
why.subtitle: You don't need an office suite to answer your phone.

cards.title: Keep your number
cards.body: No website, no widget, no new phone. You set up call forwarding on the number you already have, and that's it.

cards.title: Does one thing well
cards.body: Big software packages cost €49 to €75 a month and try to do everything. Marketplaces are free but only work in their app. HandyPlan just makes sure missed calls turn into jobs.

cards.title: Fair to your customers
cards.body: Nobody pays extra because their heating broke on a Sunday. The priority fee is a fixed amount and is shown before they book.

languages.title: In your language
languages.subtitle: Available in German and English. Arabic is coming soon.
languages.why: A lot of people in the trades grew up speaking another language. In trades like electrical engineering and metalwork it's around 30%. We haven't found another platform that offers the business side in anything but German.
languages.source: German Confederation of Skilled Crafts (ZDH), employees with a migration background in the trades (Federal Statistical Office, Microcensus)

items.a: Sign up for free and add your business details. Then set up call forwarding on your phone for the calls you can't take. From then on, every missed call gets a text back.
Yes. Text replies, job cards and booking are free. You only pay if you turn on one of the AI features, like the AI calling agent.

items.q: Do I need a website or new software?
items.a: No. HandyPlan works with the phone number you already have. You don't need a website, a booking widget or office software.

items.q: Do my customers need an app?
items.a: No. Callers get a text with a short form that opens in any browser. The customer app is optional, for people who want to search and compare tradespeople nearby.
Real emergencies need a person on the phone, so keep those on your emergency number. HandyPlan is for everyday calls, like a quote request or a routine repair.
Any business that misses calls while working. It fits especially well where there's a lot of repair and maintenance work, like heating, plumbing and electrical.
On AWS servers in Frankfurt. HandyPlan is GDPR-compliant, we have a data processing agreement (DPA) ready for you, and no customer or job data is stored in the US.
German and English. Arabic is coming soon, for your side of the app too, not only for customers.
